questions.question_english: A School Principal is investigating a serious disciplinary incident involving a violent altercation between two 14-year-old students. One student belongs to an influential, wealthy family, whereas the other was admitted under the Economically Weaker Section (EWS) quota. The influential parents demand the summary expulsion of the EWS student. Which foundational UNCRC principle must guide the Principal to ensure procedural justice and institutional integrity?
options_english: Article 2 (Non-discrimination), ensuring impartial inquiry and equal procedural treatment irrespective of socio-economic background
Article 6 (Right to life and survival), obligating the school to provide immediate financial compensation to the EWS student
Article 28 (Right to education), which strictly prohibits any form of corrective institutional discipline or investigation in school settings
Article 15 (Freedom of association), requiring the administration to permit student groups to independently resolve disciplinary matters without authority
questions.explanation_english:
The correct answer is (A). Under Article 2 of the UNCRC, the school administration is legally and ethically bound to uphold non-discrimination, ensuring that every child receives equal procedural justice irrespective of the socio-economic status, wealth, or influence of their parents.

Institutional and Legal Principles Involved:
1. Non-Discrimination (Article 2 UNCRC): Disciplinary processes in public or aided educational institutions must be objective, fact-based, and completely impervious to external pressure, wealth disparities, or social status. Treating students unequally based on family background constitutes direct discrimination.
2. Principles of Natural Justice: Both students are entitled to a fair hearing (*audi alteram partem*). An impartial inquiry must determine facts, degrees of culpability, and mitigating circumstances before any restorative or corrective action is decided.
3. Right to Education (Article 28 UNCRC & Section 17 RTE Act 2009): Disciplinary measures in schools must respect the child's human dignity and developmental needs. Summary expulsion of an EWS student under external parental pressure violates Section 17 of the RTE Act (prohibiting mental harassment and arbitrary exclusion) and contravenes the fundamental guarantee of equality under Article 14 of the Constitution of India.

2. प्राकृतिक न्याय के सिद्धांत: दोनों विद्यार्थियों को अपनी बात रखने का समान अवसर (*Audi alteram partem*) मिलना अनिवार्य है। निष्पक्ष जांच के आधार पर ही वस्तुनिष्ठ निर्णय लिया जाना चाहिए।
3. शिक्षा का अधिकार (अनुच्छेद 28 UNCRC तथा धारा 17 RTE अधिनियम 2009): विद्यालय में अनुशासन सुधारात्मक होना चाहिए, प्रतिशोधात्मक नहीं। RTE अधिनियम की धारा 17 मानसिक प्रताड़ना और मनमाने निष्कासन पर रोक लगाती है। साथ ही भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 14 (विधि के समक्ष समता) यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि आर्थिक विषमता के आधार पर न्याय से वंचित न किया जाए।

questions.question_english: Which historical document, drafted by Eglantyne Jebb in 1923 and adopted by the League of Nations in 1924, is considered the first international declaration specifically affirming child rights?
options_english: The Geneva Declaration of the Rights of the Child
The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child
The United Nations Millennium Declaration of 2000
The Hague Convention on Protection of Children
questions.explanation_english:
The Geneva Declaration of the Rights of the Child (1924) was the first international instrument specifically dedicated to child rights:

1. Origin and Drafting: Drafted in 1923 by British social reformer Eglantyne Jebb (founder of the Save the Children Fund) in response to the starvation and suffering of children across Europe following World War I.
2. Adoption: Officially adopted by the League of Nations on September 26, 1924.
3. Core Principle: The Declaration famously proclaimed that 'mankind owes to the child the best that it has to give' and set out five fundamental principles covering material support for development, priority relief in times of distress, vocational opportunities, and protection from exploitation.
4. Legacy: It served as the historic precursor to the UN Declaration of the Rights of the Child (1959) and the comprehensive, legally binding UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC, 1989).

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
बाल अधिकारों की जिनेवा घोषणा (Geneva Declaration of the Rights of the Child, 1924) बाल अधिकारों पर पहला औपचारिक अंतर्राष्ट्रीय दस्तावेज है:

1. ऐतिहासिक पृष्ठभूमि: प्रथम विश्व युद्ध के बाद यूरोप में युद्ध और भुखमरी से पीड़ित बच्चों की रक्षा के लिए 'सेव द चिल्ड्रन' (Save the Children) की संस्थापिका एग्लेनटाइन जेब (Eglantyne Jebb) ने 1923 में इसका मसौदा तैयार किया था।
2. राष्ट्र संघ द्वारा अंगीकरण: 26 सितंबर 1924 को राष्ट्र संघ (League of Nations) की महासभा ने इसे औपचारिक रूप से अंगीकृत किया।
3. मूल संदेश: इस घोषणा पत्र का सुप्रसिद्ध सिद्धांत था कि "मानवता का यह कर्तव्य है कि वह बच्चे को अपना सर्वश्रेष्ठ दे (mankind owes to the child the best that it has to give)"। इसमें बच्चों के शारीरिक-मानसिक पोषण, विपत्ति में सर्वप्रथम सहायता, रोजगार का साधन तथा शोषण से संरक्षण के पांच बुनियादी सिद्धांत दिए गए थे।
4. ऐतिहासिक महत्व: यह घोषणा पत्र 1959 की संयुक्त राष्ट्र बाल अधिकार घोषणा तथा 1989 के ऐतिहासिक यूएन बाल अधिकार अभिसमय (UNCRC) की वैधानिक आधारशिला बना।

अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (A) है।

questions.question_english: Which Optional Protocol to the UNCRC, adopted by the UN General Assembly in May 2000, places binding legal obligations on States Parties to prohibit the compulsory recruitment of individuals under 18 years of age into national armed forces?
options_english: Optional Protocol on the involvement of children in armed conflict (OPAC)
Optional Protocol on the sale of children, child prostitution and child pornography (OPSC)
Optional Protocol on a communications procedure (OPIC)
Optional Protocol on the elimination of hazardous child labor
questions.explanation_english:
The correct answer is (A). The Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of the Child on the Involvement of Children in Armed Conflict (OPAC) was adopted by the UN General Assembly on May 25, 2000, and entered into force on February 12, 2002.

Key Provisions of OPAC:
1. Age Threshold (Article 2): States Parties must ensure that persons who have not attained the age of 18 years are not compulsorily recruited into their armed forces.
2. Direct Participation (Article 1): States must take all feasible measures to ensure that members of their armed forces who have not reached the age of 18 do not take a direct part in hostilities.
3. Non-State Armed Groups (Article 4): Armed groups distinct from the armed forces of a State should not, under any circumstances, recruit or use in hostilities persons under 18 years of age.
4. Comparison with Other Protocols:
   - OPSC (2000): Addresses criminalization of sale of children, commercial sexual exploitation, and child pornography.
   - OPIC (2011): Establishes a quasi-judicial communications/complaint mechanism allowing children to petition the Committee on the Rights of the Child.
   India ratified both OPAC and OPSC on November 30, 2005.

2. युद्ध में प्रत्यक्ष भागीदारी पर रोक (अनुच्छेद 1): राज्य सभी आवश्यक कदम उठाएंगे ताकि 18 वर्ष से कम आयु के सैनिक युद्ध में प्रत्यक्ष रूप से भाग न लें।
3. गैर-राज्य सशस्त्र समूह (अनुच्छेद 4): विद्रोही या गैर-सरकारी सशस्त्र समूहों द्वारा 18 वर्ष से कम आयु के बच्चों की किसी भी रूप में भर्ती या युद्ध में उपयोग को पूर्णतः अवैध घोषित किया गया है।
4. अन्य प्रोटोकॉल से तुलना:

   - OPIC (2011): व्यक्तिगत शिकायतों हेतु एक याचिका/संचार तंत्र प्रदान करता है।
   भारत ने OPAC और OPSC दोनों का अनुसमर्थन 30 नवंबर 2005 को किया था।

questions.question_english: Upon concluding an inquiry that establishes a violation of human rights or negligence in the prevention of human rights violations by a public servant, what action is the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) empowered to take under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993?
options_english: It can directly initiate internal departmental disciplinary proceedings and impose penalties on the public servant.
It can directly register a First Information Report (FIR) and prosecute the errant public servant in a criminal court.
Recommend that the concerned Government or authority initiate prosecution or suitable disciplinary action against the public servant.
It can pass a legally binding judicial order for the immediate demotion or dismissal of the public servant.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 18 of the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) functions essentially as an inquiry, oversight, and recommendatory body rather than a punitive judicial tribunal or enforcement agency.
Key statutory provisions under Section 18 include:
1. Recommendatory Powers: Where the inquiry discloses the commission of a human rights violation or negligence in its prevention by a public servant, the Commission may recommend to the concerned Government or authority the initiation of proceedings for prosecution or other suitable disciplinary action against the concerned person (Section 18(a)(ii)).
2. Immediate Interim Relief: Under Section 18(a)(i), the Commission can recommend the grant of immediate interim relief to the victim or their family members.
3. Constitutional Remedies: Under Section 18(b), the NHRC can approach the Supreme Court (under Article 32) or the High Court (under Article 226) for directions, orders, or writs.
4. Absence of Direct Punitive Authority: The NHRC cannot directly convict, fine, penalize, demote, dismiss, or register an FIR against errant public servants. It forwards its findings to the government, which must submit an Action Taken Report (ATR) within one month.
5. Constitutional Separation of Powers: This framework upholds Article 50 (Separation of Judiciary from Executive), ensuring that investigative recommendations do not usurp judicial or executive disciplinary prerogatives.

मानवाधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम (PHRA), 1993 की धारा 18 के तहत राष्ट्रीय मानव अधिकार आयोग (NHRC) मुख्य रूप से एक जांच, निगरानी और अनुशंसात्मक (recommendatory) निकाय के रूप में कार्य करता है, न कि प्रत्यक्ष दंडात्मक या न्यायिक प्राधिकरण के रूप में।
धारा 18 के प्रमुख कानूनी प्रावधान एवं बिंदु:
1. अनुशंसा की शक्ति: जब धारा 13 के अधीन की गई जांच से यह सिद्ध होता है कि किसी लोक सेवक द्वारा मानवाधिकारों का उल्लंघन किया गया है या उसके निवारण में उपेक्षा बरती गई है, तो आयोग संबंधित सरकार या सक्षम प्राधिकारी से संबंधित व्यक्ति के विरुद्ध अभियोजन चलाने या उपयुक्त अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई शुरू करने की सिफारिश कर सकता है [धारा 18(क)(ii)]।
2. तत्काल अंतरिम राहत: धारा 18(क)(i) के तहत, आयोग पीड़ित या उसके परिजनों को तत्काल अंतरिम वित्तीय अथवा मानवीय सहायता देने की सिफारिश कर सकता है।
3. उच्चतर न्यायालयों में जाने का अधिकार: धारा 18(ख) के तहत, आयोग उचित आदेशों या रिटों हेतु सीधे उच्चतम न्यायालय (अनुच्छेद 32) या उच्च न्यायालय (अनुच्छेद 226) में याचिका प्रस्तुत कर सकता है।
4. प्रत्यक्ष दंडात्मक शक्तियों का अभाव: एनएचआरसी किसी लोक सेवक को सीधे बर्खास्त, पदावनत या दंडित नहीं कर सकता, न ही वह स्वयं एफआईआर दर्ज कर मुकदमा चला सकता है। संबंधित सरकार को एक माह के भीतर उस पर की गई कार्रवाई की रिपोर्ट (ATR) आयोग को प्रस्तुत करनी होती है।
5. संवैधानिक शक्ति संतुलन: यह व्यवस्था कार्यपालिका, न्यायपालिका और सांविधिक आयोगों के बीच शक्ति संतुलन (Separation of Powers) बनाए रखने हेतु बनाई गई है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Recommend that the concerned Government initiate prosecution or suitable action.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Upon completing an inquiry that establishes a human rights violation by a public servant, the Commission acts within its advisory mandate. Under Section 18, it recommends that the concerned government or authority initiate criminal prosecution, departmental disciplinary proceedings, or grant immediate interim relief to the victim, as direct penal enforcement remains with the state.

questions.question_english: In what manner can the Chairperson or any Member of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) be removed from office on grounds of proved misbehavior or incapacity?
options_english: By an order of the President of India, following an inquiry and report by the Supreme Court
By a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority in both Houses of Parliament (impeachment)
By the Prime Minister on the binding recommendation of the Union Cabinet
By the Chief Justice of India following an internal judicial committee inquiry
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 5(1) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, the Chairperson or any Member of the NHRC can only be removed from office by order of the President of India on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. However, the President can issue such an order only after the Supreme Court, on a reference being made to it by the President, has held an inquiry in accordance with the prescribed procedure and reported that the Chairperson or Member ought on any such ground to be removed.
Additionally, under Section 5(2), the President may remove the Chairperson or any Member without a Supreme Court inquiry if that person is adjudged an insolvent, engages in paid employment outside the duties of the office during their term, is unfit to continue by reason of infirmity of mind or body, is of unsound mind declared by a competent court, or is convicted and sentenced to imprisonment for an offense involving moral turpitude.
questions.explanation_hindi:
मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 5(1) के अनुसार, राष्ट्रीय मानव अधिकार आयोग के अध्यक्ष या किसी सदस्य को साबित कदाचार या असमर्थता के आधार पर केवल राष्ट्रपति के आदेश द्वारा ही हटाया जा सकता है। परंतु ऐसा आदेश राष्ट्रपति केवल तभी जारी कर सकते हैं जब राष्ट्रपति द्वारा इस संदर्भ में मामला भेजे जाने पर उच्चतम न्यायालय (Supreme Court) द्वारा निर्धारित प्रक्रिया के अनुसार औपचारिक जाँच की गई हो और उच्चतम न्यायालय ने अपनी रिपोर्ट में संबंधित व्यक्ति को हटाए जाने की अनुशंसा की हो।
इसके अतिरिक्त धारा 5(2) के तहत कुछ विशिष्ट परिस्थितियों (जैसे दिवालिया घोषित होना, मानसिक या शारीरिक रूप से अस्वस्थ होना, अपने पद के कर्तव्यों से इतर कोई सवेतन नियोजन करना, या नैतिक अधमता वाले अपराध में सिद्धदोष ठहराया जाना) में राष्ट्रपति सीधे भी पदमुक्त कर सकते हैं। अतः साबित कदाचार या असमर्थता के मामले में उच्चतम न्यायालय की जाँच अनिवार्य है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) By an order of the President, passed after an inquiry by the Supreme Court

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Section 5 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, the Chairperson or any Member of the Commission can only be removed from office by an order of the President of India. Such removal requires a formal inquiry conducted by the Supreme Court, which must report proved misbehavior or incapacity following due process.

गैर-भेदभाव का सिद्धांत (अनुच्छेद 2)
बालक का सर्वोत्तम हित (अनुच्छेद 3)

questions.question_english: The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) is anchored upon four core guiding principles recognized by the Committee on the Rights of the Child. Which of the following is NOT one of those four foundational principles?
options_english: Right to privacy
Non-discrimination (Article 2)
Best interests of the child (Article 3)
Right to life, survival and development (Article 6)
questions.explanation_english:
The correct answer is (A). The UN Committee on the Rights of the Child has identified four articles of the UNCRC as "General Principles" that underpin the interpretation and implementation of all other rights in the convention:

1. Article 2: Non-discrimination (guaranteeing that all rights apply to all children without distinction of any kind).
2. Article 3: Best interests of the child (mandating that in all actions concerning children, the child's best interests shall be a primary consideration).
3. Article 6: Right to life, survival and development (ensuring the maximum extent possible the survival and holistic physical, mental, spiritual, and social development of the child).
4. Article 12: Respect for the views of the child (affirming the right of the child to express opinions freely and have them taken seriously).

While the Right to Privacy is a protected human right recognized under Article 16 of the UNCRC (protecting the child against arbitrary or unlawful interference with privacy, family, home, or correspondence), it is a substantive specific right and NOT one of the four overarching constitutional principles.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर (A) है। संयुक्त राष्ट्र बाल अधिकार समिति ने UNCRC के चार अनुच्छेदों को 'सामान्य/मार्गदर्शक सिद्धांतों' (General Principles) के रूप में निर्धारित किया है, जो कन्वेंशन के सभी अन्य अनुच्छेदों की व्याख्या का आधार बनते हैं:

1. अनुच्छेद 2: गैर-भेदभाव (Non-discrimination) - बिना किसी भेदभाव के सभी बच्चों को समान अधिकार।
2. अनुच्छेद 3: बालक का सर्वोत्तम हित (Best interests of the child) - बच्चों से संबंधित सभी निर्णयों में बच्चे का हित प्राथमिक विचार होगा।
3. अनुच्छेद 6: जीवन, उत्तरजीविता और विकास का अधिकार (Right to life, survival and development) - बच्चे का सर्वांगीण शारीरिक व मानसिक विकास।
4. अनुच्छेद 12: बालक के विचारों का सम्मान (Respect for the views of the child) - बच्चे को अपने विचार व्यक्त करने और सुने जाने का अधिकार।

यद्यपि 'निजता का अधिकार' (Right to Privacy) UNCRC के अनुच्छेद 16 के तहत एक सुरक्षित विधिक अधिकार है (जो बच्चे के परिवार, घर और पत्राचार में मनमाने हस्तक्षेप से बचाता है), लेकिन यह कन्वेंशन के चार बुनियादी छत्र (Umbrella) मार्गदर्शक सिद्धांतों में सम्मिलित नहीं है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Right to privacy

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child is anchored by four foundational principles: Article 2 (Non-discrimination), Article 3 (Best interests of the child), Article 6 (Right to life, survival and development), and Article 12 (Respect for the views of the child). Privacy, while protected elsewhere in Article 16, is not a core principle.

options_hindi: मानवाधिकारों की सार्वभौम घोषणा और संयुक्त राष्ट्र का चार्टर

1949 के जिनेवा अभिसमय और उनके अतिरिक्त प्रोटोकॉल

questions.question_english: Which international covenants are specifically referred to in the statutory definition of "International Covenants" under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993?
options_english: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the Charter of the United Nations
The ICCPR and ICESCR adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1966
The Geneva Conventions of 1949 and their subsequent Additional Protocols
The Convention on the Rights of the Child and the CEDAW treaty framework
questions.explanation_english:
Section 2(1)(f) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 explicitly defines 'International Covenants' as:
"the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR) adopted by the General Assembly of the United Nations on the 16th December, 1966 and such other Covenant or Convention adopted by the General Assembly of the United Nations as the Central Government may, by notification, specify."

Context and Significance:
1. The Twin Covenants: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR, 1948) was a non-binding declaration. To create binding legal treaty obligations, the UN General Assembly adopted the ICCPR and the ICESCR on December 16, 1966. Together with the UDHR, they constitute the 'International Bill of Human Rights'.
2. India's Position: India acceded to both ICCPR and ICESCR on April 10, 1979.
3. Statutory Linkage: The PHRA, 1993 establishes a direct statutory link under Section 2(1)(d) read with Section 2(1)(f), allowing rights contained in ICCPR and ICESCR that are enforceable by Indian courts to be recognized as human rights under the Act.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 2(1)(f) में 'अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रसंविदाओं' (International Covenants) को परिभाषित किया गया है।

इस धारा के अनुसार:
"'अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रसंविदाओं' से 16 दिसंबर, 1966 को संयुक्त राष्ट्र की महासभा द्वारा अंगीकृत नागरिक और राजनीतिक अधिकारों पर अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रसंविदा (ICCPR) तथा आर्थिक, सामाजिक और सांस्कृतिक अधिकारों पर अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रसंविदा (ICESCR) अभिप्रेत हैं, और इसमें ऐसी अन्य प्रसंविदा या अभिसमय भी शामिल हैं जिन्हें केंद्र सरकार अधिसूचना द्वारा विनिर्दिष्ट करे।"

प्रमुख तथ्य:
1. अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार विधेयक: 1948 की मानवाधिकारों की सार्वभौम घोषणा (UDHR) बाध्यकारी संधि नहीं थी। अतः संयुक्त राष्ट्र महासभा ने 16 दिसंबर 1966 को दो बाध्यकारी प्रसंविदाएं—ICCPR और ICESCR अंगीकृत कीं। UDHR और ये दोनों प्रसंविदाएं मिलकर 'अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार विधेयक' (International Bill of Human Rights) बनाती हैं।
2. भारत का परिग्रहण: भारत ने 10 अप्रैल, 1979 को इन दोनों संधियों का परिग्रहण (accession) किया था।
3. विधिक महत्व: इस परिभाषा के माध्यम से भारतीय संसद ने अंतरराष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार संधियों को घरेलू मानवाधिकार अधिनियम (PHRA, 1993) के साथ सीधे विधिक रूप से संबद्ध कर दिया है।

अतः विकल्प (B) सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) The ICCPR and ICESCR adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1966

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 2(1)(f) of the Protection of Human Rights Act explicitly defines “International Covenants” as the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR), both adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in 1966 and subsequently acceded to by India.

I. यह अधिनियम राष्ट्रीय मानव अधिकार आयोग (NHRC), राज्य मानव अधिकार आयोगों (SHRCs) और मानव अधिकार न्यायालयों की स्थापना का प्रावधान करता है।

III. यह अधिनियम आयोग को उस तिथि से, जिस दिन उल्लंघन का कृत्य घटित हुआ था, एक वर्ष की समाप्ति के बाद किसी भी मामले की जांच करने से रोकता है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

केवल I और III
केवल II और III
I, II और III

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993:
I. The Act provides for the establishment of the NHRC, SHRCs, and Human Rights Courts.
II. It extends to the whole of India, but state-level human rights violations can exclusively be investigated by SHRCs.
III. The Act prohibits the Commission from inquiring into any matter after the expiry of one year from the date on which the act constituting the violation occurred.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
I and III only
II and III only
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english:
Statement I is correct:
The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 establishes a three-tier institutional protection mechanism across India:
1. National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) under Section 3 (Chapter II);
2. State Human Rights Commissions (SHRCs) under Section 21 (Chapter V); and
3. District Human Rights Courts under Section 30 (Chapter VI) designated by State Governments with the concurrence of the High Court Chief Justice.

Statement II is incorrect:
While the Act extends to the whole of India, the NHRC is not excluded from inquiring into human rights violations occurring within States. Section 36(1) bars the NHRC from inquiring into matters pending before a State Commission or another statutory commission, but the NHRC maintains nationwide concurrent jurisdiction to take cognizance of human rights violations anywhere in India unless already seized by an SHRC. Furthermore, under Section 21(5), if the NHRC is already inquiring into a matter, the State Commission is prohibited from inquiring into it.

Statement III is correct:
Section 36(2) provides an express limitation period:
"The Commission or the State Commission shall not inquire into any matter after the expiry of one year from the date on which the act constituting violation of human rights is alleged to have been committed."
Thus, complaints brought after the expiry of one year from the date of the alleged incident are time-barred.

Therefore, only Statements I and III are correct, making Option (B) the correct choice.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कथन I सही है:
मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 देश में त्रि-स्तरीय संस्थागत तंत्र का गठन करता है:
1. राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर 'राष्ट्रीय मानव अधिकार आयोग' (धारा 3);
2. राज्य स्तर पर 'राज्य मानव अधिकार आयोग' (धारा 21); और
3. प्रत्येक जिले में त्वरित सुनवाई के लिए सत्र न्यायालय को 'मानव अधिकार न्यायालय' (धारा 30) के रूप में विनिर्दिष्ट करने का प्रावधान।

कथन II गलत है:
यह कथन गलत है कि राज्य-स्तरीय मामलों की जांच केवल राज्य आयोग ही कर सकते हैं। धारा 21(5) के तहत, यदि किसी मामले की जांच NHRC कर रहा है, तो राज्य आयोग उसमें जांच नहीं करेगा। धारा 36(1) के अनुसार NHRC केवल उन मामलों की जांच नहीं करता जो किसी राज्य आयोग या अन्य आयोग के समक्ष पहले से लंबित हैं। यदि कोई मामला राज्य आयोग के समक्ष लंबित नहीं है, तो NHRC पूरे देश में (किसी भी राज्य में) घटित मानवाधिकार उल्लंघन का संज्ञान ले सकता है।

कथन III सही है:
धारा 36(2) में जांच के लिए एक वर्ष की स्पष्ट परिसीमा (limitation period) निर्धारित की गई है:
"आयोग या राज्य आयोग ऐसे किसी मामले की जांच नहीं करेगा जो उस तारीख से, जिसको मानवाधिकार का उल्लंघन करने वाला कार्य किया जाना कथित है, एक वर्ष की समाप्ति के पश्चात संज्ञान में लाया गया हो।"

अतः केवल कथन I और III सही हैं, इसलिए विकल्प (B) सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Protection of Human Rights Act provides the legal foundation for establishing the National Human Rights Commission, State Commissions, and District Human Rights Courts. Furthermore, Section 36(2) strictly limits inquiries by prohibiting the Commission from taking cognizance of any violation reported after one year from its occurrence. Central and state jurisdictions remain distinct.

questions.question_english: The 'International Bill of Human Rights' consists of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) alongside two legally binding multilateral covenants adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1966. Which are these two core covenants?
options_english: The Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) and the Convention Against Torture (CAT)
The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR)
The Geneva Conventions of 1949 and the Hague Conventions of 1907
The Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW) and the 1951 Refugee Convention
questions.explanation_english:
The 'International Bill of Human Rights' is the authoritative legal collective term for the three foundational instruments of international human rights law:
1. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR, adopted in 1948) - the non-binding moral foundation.
2. The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR, adopted December 16, 1966; entered into force March 23, 1976), along with its two Optional Protocols (on individual complaints and abolition of the death penalty).
3. The International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR, adopted December 16, 1966; entered into force January 3, 1976), along with its Optional Protocol.
- Together, these two 1966 covenants transformed the broad moral and political principles of the 1948 UDHR into legally binding treaty commitments for ratifying States Parties.
- Relevance to India: India acceded to both the ICCPR and ICESCR on April 10, 1979. Under Section 2(1)(f) of the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993, the term 'International Covenants' is specifically defined as the ICCPR and ICESCR adopted by the UN General Assembly on December 16, 1966, establishing their foundational statutory status under Indian law.
questions.explanation_hindi:
'मानवाधिकारों का अंतर्राष्ट्रीय बिल' (International Bill of Human Rights) अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार कानून के तीन बुनियादी घटकों का आधिकारिक समुच्चय है:
1. सार्वभौमिक मानवाधिकार घोषणापत्र (UDHR, 1948) - आधारभूत नैतिक घोषणा।
2. नागरिक और राजनीतिक अधिकारों पर अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रसंविदा (ICCPR, अंगीकृत 1966; प्रभावी 1976), इसके दो ऐच्छिक प्रोटोकॉल सहित।
3. आर्थिक, सामाजिक और सांस्कृतिक अधिकारों पर अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रसंविदा (ICESCR, अंगीकृत 1966; प्रभावी 1976), इसके ऐच्छिक प्रोटोकॉल सहित।
- 1966 की इन दोनों प्रसंविदाओं ने 1948 के UDHR के सिद्धांतों को कानूनी रूप से बाध्यकारी संधियों में परिवर्तित किया।
- भारत के संदर्भ में महत्व: भारत ने 10 अप्रैल, 1979 को ICCPR और ICESCR दोनों का अनुसमर्थन किया था। भारत के 'मानवाधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम (PHRA), 1993' की धारा 2(1)(च) [Section 2(1)(f)] में 'अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रसंविदाओं' (International Covenants) को स्पष्ट रूप से 16 दिसंबर, 1966 को अंगीकृत ICCPR और ICESCR के रूप में ही परिभाषित किया गया है, जो भारत में मानवाधिकारों की विधिक नींव है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The International Bill of Human Rights consists of three essential foundational components: the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights. Together, these complementary instruments convert aspirational global human rights standards into legally binding commitments for ratifying nation-states.

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 3(4) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, there is a Secretary-General who is the Chief Executive Officer of the Commission and exercises such powers and discharges such functions of the Commission (other than judicial functions and the power to make regulations under Section 40B) as may be delegated by the Commission or the Chairperson. While the Chairperson is the institutional head and guides the policy and judicial functioning, the Secretary-General (an officer of the rank of Secretary to the Government of India) functions as the administrative head responsible for day-to-day administrative machinery and executive implementation.

questions.question_english: Under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, what procedure is prescribed if the Commission considers it necessary to investigate a complaint against a public servant?
options_english: The Commission must mandatorily obtain prior formal sanction for prosecution from the Central Government
Utilize the services of officers or investigation agencies of the Central or State Government with their concurrence
The Commission must transfer the complaint immediately to the Central Bureau of Investigation
The Commission is statutorily barred from directly investigating complaints against public servants
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 14 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, the Commission is empowered to conduct investigations through central and state agencies:

1. Section 14(1) Statutory Provision: 'The Commission may, for the purpose of conducting any inquiry under this Act, utilise the services of any officer or investigation agency of the Central Government or any State Government with the concurrence of the Central Government or the State Government, as the case may be.'
2. Powers of Investigating Personnel (Section 14(2)): Any officer or agency whose services are utilized shall investigate under the direction and supervision of the Commission and possesses the power to summon persons, examine witnesses, require document production, and requisition public records.
3. Independent Investigation Division: While the NHRC maintains its own internal investigative wing headed by a Director General of Police (DGP), Section 14 provides statutory authority to requisition officers from other state and central agencies with governmental concurrence.
4. No Prior Sanction Required for Inquiry: Section 14 does not require the Commission to seek prior prosecution sanction under Section 197 CrPC simply to initiate an inquiry or investigation; the Commission is an independent statutory inquiring body.

Therefore, Option (B) accurately reflects the statutory procedure under Section 14.
questions.explanation_hindi:
मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 14 "अन्वेषण हेतु अधिकारियों और अन्वेषण एजेंसियों की सेवाएं लेने" का प्रावधान करती है।

धारा 14(1) के अनुसार:
"आयोग, इस अधिनियम के अधीन कोई जांच करने के प्रयोजन के लिए, यथास्थिति, केंद्र सरकार या राज्य सरकार की सहमति (concurrence) से केंद्र सरकार या किसी राज्य सरकार के किसी अधिकारी या अन्वेषण एजेंसी की सेवाओं का उपयोग कर सकेगा।"

विधिक बिंदु:
1. जांच अधिकारियों की शक्तियां (धारा 14(2)): जब किसी अधिकारी या एजेंसी की सेवाएं ली जाती हैं, तो वह आयोग के अधीक्षण और निदेश के अधीन कार्य करता है। उसे गवाहों को समन करने, उनकी परीक्षा करने, दस्तावेज प्रस्तुत कराने और सार्वजनिक अभिलेख मंगवाने की शक्तियां प्राप्त होती हैं।
2. आंतरिक एवं बाह्य जांच तंत्र: NHRC के पास पुलिस महानिदेशक (DGP) के नेतृत्व में अपना एक स्वतंत्र अन्वेषण प्रभाग होता है, किंतु जटिल मामलों में वह धारा 14 के तहत संबंधित सरकार की सहमति से राज्य पुलिस, CID या केंद्रीय एजेंसियों के अधिकारियों की सेवाएं ले सकता है।
3. जांच हेतु पूर्व स्वीकृति अनावश्यक: आयोग को लोक सेवकों के विरुद्ध जांच का आदेश देने के लिए सरकार से पूर्व अभियोजन स्वीकृति (sanction) लेने की आवश्यकता नहीं होती।

अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (B) है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Utilize services of Central or State government officers/agencies with concurrence.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Section 14 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, when inquiring into violations committed by public servants, the Commission can utilize the services of officers or investigation agencies belonging to the Central or State Governments, subject to obtaining the formal concurrence of the concerned government authority controlling those investigative staff services.

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The definition of "Human Rights" under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 strictly limits the NHRC to enforcing only those rights explicitly enumerated in the Fundamental Rights chapter (Part III) of the Indian Constitution.
Reason (R): The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 defines human rights as rights relating to life, liberty, equality, and dignity guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in International Covenants enforceable by courts in India.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english:
Assertion (A) is false:
The mandate of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) is not restricted solely to Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution. Under Section 2(1)(d) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, human rights include:
1. Rights guaranteed by the Constitution as a whole (which includes constitutional rights beyond Part III, such as Article 300A, and Directive Principles read organically into Article 21);
2. Rights embodied in the International Covenants (ICCPR and ICESCR) that are enforceable by courts in India. The Supreme Court of India in cases such as Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan and D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal has repeatedly affirmed that international covenant norms can be applied domestically, and the NHRC actively intervenes across this broader spectrum. Thus, Assertion (A) is incorrect.

Reason (R) is true:
Section 2(1)(d) of the Act verbatim defines human rights as: 'the rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity of the individual guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in the International Covenants and enforceable by courts in India.'

Since Assertion (A) is false while Reason (R) is true, Option (D) is the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
अभिकथन (A) गलत है:
राष्ट्रीय मानव अधिकार आयोग (NHRC) का अधिकार क्षेत्र केवल भारतीय संविधान के भाग III (मौलिक अधिकार) तक ही सीमित नहीं है। मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 2(1)(d) में मानवाधिकारों की एक व्यापक परिभाषा दी गई है, जिसमें:

कारण (R) सही है:

questions.question_english: Human rights are fundamentally rooted in the principle that they inhere in all individuals simply by virtue of their humanity. Which of the following constitutes a core defining characteristic of human rights?
options_english: They are inalienable, universal, and non-discriminatory.
They are bestowed by the State and subject to arbitrary revocation by the government.
They are contingent privileges earned through the fulfillment of civic duties.
They are confined exclusively to citizens residing in democratic nations.
questions.explanation_english: Human rights belong to every individual by virtue of being human, regardless of legal status, nationality, ethnicity, gender, or religion. As defined under Section 2(1)(d) of India's Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993, 'human rights' means the rights relating to life, liberty, equality, and dignity of the individual guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in the International Covenants and enforceable by courts in India. Human rights are not privileges bestowed by the State that can be arbitrarily withdrawn or revoked; rather, they are inherent to every human being from birth. Consequently, their defining characteristics are: (1) Universality—they apply equally and without discrimination to all people everywhere (as recognized in Articles 1 and 2 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, 1948); (2) Inalienability—they cannot be surrendered, taken away, or stripped from any person except through strictly prescribed due process of law; and (3) Indivisibility and Interdependence—civil, political, economic, social, and cultural rights are inherently intertwined, and one set of rights cannot be fully realized without the other.
questions.explanation_hindi: मानवाधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम (PHRA), 1993 की धारा 2(1)(घ) [Section 2(1)(d)] के अनुसार, 'मानवाधिकार' से तात्पर्य संविधान द्वारा प्रत्याभूत या अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रसंविदाओं में सन्निहित तथा भारत में न्यायालयों द्वारा प्रवर्तनीय व्यक्ति के जीवन, स्वतंत्रता, समानता और गरिमा से संबंधित अधिकारों से है। मानवाधिकार राज्य द्वारा प्रदत्त कोई रियायत या विशेषाधिकार नहीं हैं, बल्कि ये मानव होने के नाते प्रत्येक व्यक्ति में जन्मजात अंतर्निहित होते हैं। इसलिए इनकी प्रमुख निर्णायक विशेषताएं हैं: (1) सार्वभौमिकता (Universal)—ये दुनिया के प्रत्येक कोने में सभी मनुष्यों पर समान रूप से लागू होते हैं; (2) अहस्तांतरणीयता (Inalienable)—इन्हें किसी भी व्यक्ति से छीना, स्थानांतरित या त्यागा नहीं जा सकता; तथा (3) गैर-भेदभावपूर्ण (Non-discriminatory)—ये धर्म, मूलवंश, जाति, लिंग, जन्मस्थान या राष्ट्रीयता के आधार पर किसी भी प्रकार के भेदभाव के बिना सभी को प्राप्त होते हैं (जैसा कि सार्वभौमिक मानवाधिकार घोषणापत्र, 1948 के अनुच्छेद 1 और 2 में घोषित किया गया है)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) They are inalienable, universal, and non-discriminatory.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Human rights belong to every individual by virtue of being human, regardless of legal status, nationality, or ethnicity. They are universal because they apply to everyone everywhere, inalienable because they cannot be stripped away or surrendered, and non-discriminatory because they guarantee equal treatment and protection for all people without exception or prejudice.

questions.question_english: A female teacher employed on a contractual basis in a government-aided school submits an application for statutory maternity leave. The school managing committee rejects the application, asserting that maternity benefits are strictly restricted to regular, permanent personnel. As an educational administrator cognizant of human rights jurisprudence and statutory labor enactments, how must this matter be resolved under prevailing judicial precedents?
options_english: Uphold the management's rejection, as contractual employees are categorically exempted from statutory welfare entitlements.
Sanction the maternity leave, as maternity protection is an integral facet of Article 21 and applies equally to contractual staff.
Advise the pregnant teacher to resign from service, deliver the infant, and subsequently seek re-employment against future vacancies.
Grant an informal compromise of 12 weeks of unpaid leave without pay or employment security.
questions.explanation_english: In landmark constitutional precedents—notably Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Female Workers (Muster Roll) (2000) 3 SCC 224, Dr. Kavita Yadav v. The Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (2023), and numerous High Court judgments concerning contractual teachers—the Supreme Court of India categorically established that maternity benefits under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 cannot be denied to female employees on the grounds that they are employed on a contractual, temporary, ad-hoc, or daily-wage basis. The apex court affirmed that maternity protection and childbearing are inextricably intertwined with human dignity, bodily integrity, and the right to life with dignity guaranteed under Article 21, read with Article 42 of the Constitution. Denying maternity leave to contractual teachers violates both statutory welfare legislation and constitutional human rights principles. Therefore, the school management is legally obligated to grant full statutory maternity leave.
questions.explanation_hindi: सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने 'दिल्ली नगर निगम बनाम महिला कर्मचारी (मस्टर रोल)' (2000) और 'डॉ. कविता यादव बनाम सचिव, स्वास्थ्य एवं परिवार कल्याण मंत्रालय' (2023) सहित कई ऐतिहासिक मामलों में यह सुदृढ़ रूप से स्थापित किया है कि मातृत्व लाभ अधिनियम, 1961 के तहत मिलने वाले लाभ संविदात्मक (contractual), तदर्थ या दैनिक वेतनभोगी महिला कर्मचारियों को केवल इस आधार पर नकारा नहीं जा सकता कि वे स्थायी सेवा में नहीं हैं। शीर्ष अदालत ने माना है कि मातृत्व संरक्षण भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 21 के तहत प्रदत्त गरिमापूर्ण जीवन के अधिकार और अनुच्छेद 42 (प्रसूति सहायता) का अभिन्न अंग है। अतः किसी सहायता प्राप्त या सरकारी स्कूल का प्रबंधन कानूनी रूप से संविदा शिक्षिका को मातृत्व अवकाश देने से इनकार नहीं कर सकता, और शैक्षिक प्रशासक को विधिक रूप से मातृत्व अवकाश स्वीकृत करने का आदेश देना चाहिए।

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Supreme Court of India has ruled that maternity protection is an essential facet of human dignity under Article 21. Statutory maternity benefits cannot be denied to female employees simply because they hold contractual or temporary appointments, obligating employers to grant full statutory maternity leave regardless of formal employment contract classifications.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the statutory functions and powers of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993:
I. It can intervene in any legal proceeding involving allegations of human rights violations pending before a court, subject to the approval of such court.
II. It can visit any jail or other custodial institution under the control of a State Government to inspect the living conditions of the inmates.
III. It can review constitutional and legal safeguards for the protection of human rights and recommend measures for their effective implementation.
IV. It can directly impose financial penalties and levy fines on State Governments that fail to implement its recommendations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I, II and III only
I, III and IV only
II, III and IV only
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 12 of the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993:
- Statement I is correct: Under Section 12(b), the NHRC has the power to intervene in any proceeding involving any allegation of violation of human rights pending before a court, with the approval of such court.
- Statement II is correct: Under Section 12(c), the NHRC can visit, notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, any jail or other institution under the control of the State Government, where persons are detained or lodged, to study the living conditions of the inmates and make recommendations thereon.
- Statement III is correct: Under Section 12(d), the Commission can review the safeguards provided by or under the Constitution or any law for the time being in force for the protection of human rights and recommend measures for their effective implementation.
- Statement IV is incorrect: The NHRC has no statutory power to adjudicate criminal penalties, levy fines, or directly enforce financial penalties against State Governments. Its recommendations under Section 18 are advisory, though State authorities are required to submit action taken reports or reasons for non-compliance, and the Commission can approach the High Courts or the Supreme Court for appropriate writs and enforcement.
Therefore, only statements I, II, and III are correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:
मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम (PHRA), 1993 की धारा 12 के अंतर्गत आयोग के कार्यों का विस्तृत विवरण दिया गया है:
- कथन I सही है: धारा 12(ख) के अनुसार, आयोग किसी न्यायालय की अनुमति से उस न्यायालय के समक्ष लंबित मानव अधिकार उल्लंघन से जुड़ी किसी भी कार्यवाही में हस्तक्षेप (intervene) कर सकता है।
- कथन II सही है: धारा 12(ग) के तहत आयोग बंदियों की रहन-सहन की दशाओं का अध्ययन करने और सुधार के उपाय सुझाने के लिए राज्य सरकार के नियंत्रणाधीन किसी जेल, हिरासत केंद्र या अन्य सुधार गृह का दौरा कर सकता है।
- कथन III सही है: धारा 12(घ) के तहत आयोग संविधान या किसी अन्य कानून के तहत मानव अधिकारों के संरक्षण के लिए उपलब्ध उपायों व सुरक्षा प्रावधानों की समीक्षा कर सकता है और उनके प्रभावी क्रियान्वयन की सिफारिश कर सकता है।
- कथन IV गलत है: NHRC के पास राज्य सरकारों पर सीधे वित्तीय जुर्माना (Financial Penalties) लगाने या दंडात्मक आदेश पारित करने की कोई वैधानिक शक्ति नहीं है। धारा 18 के अंतर्गत आयोग के निष्कर्ष और सिफारिशें सलाहकारी प्रकृति की होती हैं, यद्यपि अनुपालन न होने पर आयोग उच्च न्यायालय या उच्चतम न्यायालय में याचिका दायर कर सकता है।
अतः केवल कथन I, II और III सही हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I, II and III

However, it lacks statutory authority to impose direct financial penalties on state governments for non- compliance.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following pedagogical strategies in a school setting:
I. Role-playing landmark historical events of civil rights and social justice movements.
II. Teacher-led passive rote memorization and mechanical recitation of the articles of the UN Charter.
III. Collaborative analysis and classroom discussion of contemporary news reports on child labor and exploitation.
IV. Organizing participatory student-led Mock United Nations (MUN) General Assembly sessions.
Which of the above are effective, participatory pedagogical strategies for Human Rights Education (HRE) in a classroom?
options_english: I, II and III only
I, III and IV only
II, III and IV only
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation_english:
Human Rights Education (HRE) pedagogy emphasizes active, participatory, learner-centered, and experiential learning methods rather than passive, banking-concept education (as famously critiqued by Paulo Freire).

Evaluation of the strategies:
1. Strategy I (Role-playing): Role-playing historical struggles (e.g., Mahatma Gandhi's satyagraha, Rosa Parks, Nelson Mandela, anti-untouchability movements) promotes empathy, perspective-taking, emotional engagement, and deep historical understanding. (Effective & participatory)
2. Strategy II (Rote memorization): Mechanical recitation and rote learning of legalistic treaties or the UN Charter treats human rights as dead, abstract legal doctrine rather than lived values. It fails to develop critical thinking, attitudes, or values. (Ineffective & non-participatory)
3. Strategy III (Analyzing news on child labor): Case studies of real-world violations (such as child labor in firecracker industries or domestic servitude) connect classroom learning with Article 24 of the Constitution, Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016, and UNCRC, fostering critical inquiry and social conscience. (Effective & participatory)
4. Strategy IV (Mock UN / Youth Parliaments): Mock assemblies allow students to research diverse global perspectives, debate human rights resolutions, practice negotiation, consensus-building, and public speaking. (Effective & participatory)

Thus, strategies I, III, and IV are participatory and effective.
questions.explanation_hindi:
मानवाधिकार शिक्षा (HRE) की शिक्षण पद्धति सक्रिय, शिक्षार्थी-केंद्रित, संवादात्मक और अनुभवात्मक (Experiential) अधिगम पर बल देती है, न कि निष्क्रिय रटने पर।

रणनीतियों का मूल्यांकन:
1. रणनीति I (ऐतिहासिक आंदोलनों का रोल-प्ले): नागरिक अधिकार आंदोलनों (जैसे गांधीजी का सत्याग्रह, डॉ. बी.आर. अम्बेडकर का महाड़ सत्याग्रह, नेल्सन मंडेला का रंगभेद विरोधी संघर्ष) का नाटक या रोल-प्ले विद्यार्थियों में सहानुभूति, ऐतिहासिक चेतना और न्याय की भावना जाग्रत करता है। (प्रभावी एवं सहभागी)
2. रणनीति II (यांत्रिक रट्टा मारना): संयुक्त राष्ट्र चार्टर या कानूनी धाराओं को बिना समझे कंठस्थ करना एक निष्क्रिय पद्धति है जो बच्चों में न तो विश्लेषणात्मक चिंतन पैदा करती है और न ही मानवाधिकारों के प्रति संवेदनशीलता। यह HRE के मूल सिद्धांतों के विपरीत है। (अप्रभावी)
3. रणनीति III (बाल श्रम के समाचारों का विश्लेषण): वास्तविक जीवन की घटनाओं (जैसे बाल श्रम, बाल तस्करी) पर परिचर्चा करने से विद्यार्थी भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 24, बाल श्रम निषेध अधिनियम तथा जमीनी वास्तविकताओं को समझ पाते हैं और सामाजिक सरोकारों से जुड़ते हैं। (प्रभावी एवं सहभागी)
4. रणनीति IV (मॉक यूएन / युवा संसद): बाल संसद या मॉक यूएन के आयोजन से विद्यार्थियों में वाद-विवाद, तार्किक चिंतन, दूसरों के दृष्टिकोण को समझने और कूटनीतिक समाधान खोजने का व्यावहारिक कौशल विकसित होता है। (प्रभावी एवं सहभागी)

अतः I, III और IV प्रभावी और सहभागी रणनीतियाँ हैं। सही उत्तर विकल्प (B) है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I, III and IV

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Participatory methodologies in Human Rights Education actively engage students through experiential learning. Role-playing civil rights movements, analyzing real-world child labor news, and organizing mock UN assemblies foster critical thinking, empathy, and practical understanding. Conversely, teacher-led rote learning of legal texts remains a passive, non-participatory instructional technique inconsistent with active HRE.

questions.question_english: What fundamental paradigm shift in human rights law and jurisprudence was formalized by the adoption of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) regarding the status of the child?
options_english: Shifting the perception of the child from a passive object of charity and welfare to an autonomous legal subject and holder of rights
Transitioning the child from being parental property to becoming the exclusive legal ward and property of the state
Transferring the responsibility of child-rearing completely from biological families to state educational institutions
Replacing all sovereign domestic family laws with mandatory international juvenile justice frameworks
questions.explanation_english:
The correct answer is (A). The adoption of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) in 1989 formalized a revolutionary shift from the "welfare/charity model" to the "rights-based model" in international jurisprudence.

Key dimensions of this paradigm shift include:
1. From Needs to Rights: Historically (as in the 1924 Geneva Declaration and 1959 UN Declaration of the Rights of the Child), children were viewed merely as passive recipients of adult benevolence, charity, and protection, or as property of parents/guardians. The UNCRC established that children are distinct, autonomous human beings possessing inherent fundamental human rights that states, parents, and institutions are legally obligated to respect and fulfill.
2. Autonomous Rights-Holders: Children are no longer seen as mini-adults or future citizens in waiting, but as current citizens and subjects of law entitled to dignity, integrity, freedom of expression (Article 12), and protection from harm (Article 19).
3. State as Duty-Bearer: This paradigm shift transforms the state and society from benevolent providers into accountable "duty-bearers," legally bound to create the legislative, executive, and judicial conditions necessary for every child to realize their rights.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर (A) है। वर्ष 1989 में UNCRC को अंगीकार किए जाने से अंतरराष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार न्यायशास्त्र में 'कल्याण/परोपकार दृष्टिकोण' (Welfare/Charity Model) से 'अधिकार-आधारित दृष्टिकोण' (Rights-Based Model) की ओर एक युगांतरकारी परिवर्तन आया।

इस वैचारिक परिवर्तन के प्रमुख आयाम:
1. आवश्यकताओं से अधिकारों की ओर: 1989 से पूर्व (जैसे 1924 की जिनेवा घोषणा और 1959 की घोषणा में) बच्चों को केवल वयस्कों की कृपा, परोपकार और संरक्षण का असहाय पात्र या माता-पिता की निजी संपत्ति माना जाता था। UNCRC ने औपचारिक रूप से स्थापित किया कि प्रत्येक बालक जन्म से ही मौलिक मानवाधिकारों का स्वतंत्र एवं स्वायत्त धारक (Rights-Holder) है।
2. गरिमा और नागरिकता: बच्चे भविष्य के नागरिक मात्र नहीं हैं, बल्कि वे वर्तमान में ही गरिमा, विचार अभिव्यक्ति (अनुच्छेद 12) और शारीरिक अखंडता के विधिक हकदार हैं।
3. राज्य का विधिक दायित्व: इस परिवर्तन ने राज्य को दयालु संरक्षक के स्थान पर एक जवाबदेह 'कर्तव्य-धारक' (Duty-Bearer) बना दिया, जो बच्चों के अधिकारों को बिना किसी भेदभाव के लागू करने के लिए विधिक रूप से बाध्य है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Shifting the perception of the child from a passive object of charity and welfare to an autonomous legal subject and holder of rights

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: to a subject of legal rights. The adoption of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child marked a major legal shift from viewing children merely as passive objects of charity or parental property to recognizing them as active individual subjects possessing fundamental human rights. This model establishes children as autonomous rights-holders entitled to dignity, protection, and participation.

questions.question_english: The Chairperson and Members of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) are appointed by the President of India on the recommendations of a high-powered selection committee. Who among the following is NOT a member of this selection committee?
options_english: The Prime Minister
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha (House of the People)
The Union Minister of Home Affairs
The Chief Justice of India
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 4(1) of the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993, the Chairperson and Members of the NHRC are appointed by the President of India by warrant under his hand and seal, upon the recommendation of a six-member committee consisting of: (1) The Prime Minister (who acts as the Chairperson of the Committee); (2) The Speaker of the House of the People (Lok Sabha); (3) The Minister in-charge of the Ministry of Home Affairs in the Government of India; (4) The Leader of the Opposition in the House of the People; (5) The Leader of the Opposition in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha); and (6) The Deputy Chairman of the Council of States. The Chief Justice of India is NOT a member of this committee. However, the first proviso to Section 4(1) mandates that no sitting Judge of the Supreme Court or sitting Chief Justice of a High Court shall be appointed except after consultation with the Chief Justice of India.
questions.explanation_hindi: मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993 की धारा 4(1) के अनुसार, राष्ट्रीय मानव अधिकार आयोग के अध्यक्ष और सदस्यों की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति द्वारा अपने हस्ताक्षर और मुद्रा युक्त अधिपत्र द्वारा 6-सदस्यीय उच्चाधिकार प्राप्त चयन समिति की सिफारिशों के आधार पर की जाती है। इस चयन समिति में निम्नलिखित शामिल होते हैं: (1) प्रधान मंत्री (समिति के अध्यक्ष), (2) लोकसभा अध्यक्ष, (3) केंद्रीय गृह मंत्री, (4) लोकसभा में विपक्ष के नेता, (5) राज्यसभा में विपक्ष के नेता, तथा (6) राज्यसभा के उपसभापति। भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश (CJI) इस चयन समिति के सदस्य नहीं होते हैं। यद्यपि, धारा 4(1) के परंतुक के अनुसार यदि किसी आसीन (sitting) उच्चतम न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश या उच्च न्यायालय के मुख्य न्यायाधीश को नियुक्त करना हो, तो भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश से परामर्श आवश्यक होता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) The Chief Justice of India

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Section 4 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, the Chairperson and members of the National Human Rights Commission are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a six-member selection committee. This committee includes the Prime Minister, House Speaker, Union Home Minister, Opposition Leaders, and Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha, excluding the Chief Justice.

questions.question_english: Which of the following infrastructural deficiencies in a school constitutes a severe infringement of an adolescent girl child's right to education, health, and dignity, frequently resulting in high absenteeism and dropout rates upon attaining puberty?
options_english: Complete absence of a specialized modern digital computer laboratory
Absence of separate, secure, and functional sanitation/toilet facilities for girls
Unavailability of female drivers for designated school bus transport fleets
Standard co-educational seating arrangements within general classrooms
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 19 read with the Schedule of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, every school is legally required to fulfill prescribed norms and standards, including 'separate toilets for boys and girls' with adequate water supply and hygiene. In the landmark Supreme Court ruling in Environmental & Consumer Protection Foundation v. Delhi Administration & Ors. (2012), the apex court unequivocally held that providing clean, potable drinking water and separate functional toilets for girls and boys is an integral component of the Right to Education under Article 21A of the Constitution. The lack of private, clean, and functioning toilets severely compromises menstrual hygiene management (MHM), infringes upon the girl child's bodily privacy and dignity under Article 21, and forces adolescent girls to remain absent or permanently drop out of school, thereby defeating the mandate of universal child education.
questions.explanation_hindi: निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार (RTE) अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 19 के साथ पठित अनुसूची के तहत प्रत्येक विद्यालय के लिए बालकों और बालिकाओं हेतु 'पृथक एवं क्रियाशील शौचालय' तथा स्वच्छ पेयजल की व्यवस्था करना एक अनिवार्य कानूनी मानदंड है। सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने 'एनवायरनमेंटल एंड कंज्यूमर प्रोटेक्शन फाउंडेशन बनाम दिल्ली प्रशासन व अन्य (2012)' के ऐतिहासिक फैसले में स्पष्ट रूप से निर्देश दिया था कि बालिकाओं के लिए अलग और सुरक्षित क्रियाशील शौचालयों का अभाव संविधान के अनुच्छेद 21A के तहत शिक्षा के मूल अधिकार का हनन है। शौचालयों की अनुपलब्धता से मासिक धर्म स्वच्छता प्रबंधन (MHM) प्रभावित होता है, बालिकाओं की गरिमा और निजता (अनुच्छेद 21) भंग होती है तथा किशोरावस्था में बालिकाओं का स्कूल छोड़ना (ड्रॉपआउट) बढ़ जाता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Absence of separate, functional toilet facilities for girls

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The structural absence of separate, functional, and hygienic toilet facilities for female students severely violates their rights to health, dignity, and education. This infrastructure deficiency creates significant safety and privacy concerns during menstruation, directly driving high female student absenteeism and drop-out rates during adolescence in many developing educational systems.

questions.question_english: In the jurisprudence of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC), what does the foundational concept of "evolving capacities" (enshrined in Article 5) legally signify?
options_english: Parental direction and guidance in the exercise of rights must be calibrated progressively in harmony with the child's developing maturity and understanding
Children must automatically be granted complete adult legal emancipation and civil autonomy immediately upon biological puberty
A child's physical growth and biometric measurements directly define their penal liabilities and legal obligations
School administrations are mandated to proportionately increase academic course loads as children advance in chronological age
questions.explanation_english:
The correct answer is (A). The principle of "evolving capacities" under Article 5 of the UNCRC is a cornerstone of modern child rights law, balancing protective guidance with children's emerging autonomy.

Legal Dimensions of Article 5:
1. Article 5 Text: States Parties shall respect the responsibilities, rights, and duties of parents (or legal guardians) "to provide, in a manner consistent with the evolving capacities of the child, appropriate direction and guidance in the exercise by the child of the rights recognized in the present Convention."
2. Dynamic Balance: The concept recognizes that children are not static; as they grow and mature cognitively, emotionally, and morally, the degree of parental direction must decrease, while the child's independent exercise of their own agency, decision-making, and rights must increase.
3. Synergistic Link with Article 12: Article 5 operates in direct harmony with Article 12 (respect for the views of the child in accordance with age and maturity). It rejects both paternalistic authoritarianism (treating the child as having no voice) and premature abandonment (depriving the child of necessary adult guidance before they are ready).
4. Common Law Correlate: This mirrors the landmark common law doctrine of *Gillick competence*, which holds that parental rights yield to the child's right to make their own decisions as the child achieves sufficient understanding and intelligence.

अनुच्छेद 5 के प्रमुख विधिक आयाम:
1. विधिक प्रावधान: राज्य पक्षकार माता-पिता या विधिक अभिभावकों के दायित्वों और अधिकारों का सम्मान करेंगे कि वे "बालक की विकासशील क्षमताओं के अनुरूप" कन्वेंशन में प्रदत्त अधिकारों के प्रयोग में उचित मार्गदर्शन और निर्देशन प्रदान करें।
2. गतिशील संतुलन: यह सिद्धांत स्वीकार करता है कि बालक का विकास निरंतर होता है। जैसे-जैसे बच्चे की मानसिक, भावनात्मक और बौद्धिक परिपक्वता बढ़ती है, माता-पिता के प्रत्यक्ष नियंत्रण में कमी आनी चाहिए और बच्चे द्वारा अपने अधिकारों व निर्णयों के स्वतंत्र प्रयोग को बढ़ावा मिलना चाहिए।
3. अनुच्छेद 12 से संबंध: यह अनुच्छेद 12 (बालक के विचारों का सम्मान) का पूरक है। यह माता-पिता के निरंकुश प्राधिकार को खारिज करता है और बच्चे को उसकी परिपक्वता के अनुसार निर्णय प्रक्रिया में भागीदार बनाता है।
4. गिलिक सक्षमता (Gillick Competence): कॉमन लॉ का प्रसिद्ध 'गिलिक सिद्धांत' भी यही प्रतिपादित करता है कि जैसे-जैसे बच्चा पर्याप्त समझ और विवेक प्राप्त करता जाता है, माता-पिता का नियंत्रण समाप्त होकर बच्चे की स्वतंत्र सहमति का अधिकार प्रभावी हो जाता है।
